subject.title: Feature/Fix: Add conservative lineage safety and promotion controls

question: Should CodexBar adopt this four-PR lineage architecture as the long-term authoritative accounting path, keep it shadow-only, or prefer the narrower incremental approach in https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118?
rationale: Both approaches address real fork-accounting failures, but they establish different maintenance and promotion boundaries; tests cannot determine which permanent architecture the project intends to support.

options.title: Adopt the lineage stack
options.body: Review and land the dependency stack in order after exact-head frozen-corpus proof confirms compatibility, bounded operation, authorization transitions, and rollback.

options.title: Keep lineage shadow-only
options.body: Merge only the non-authoritative comparison and diagnostic seams while retaining the existing scanner as the permanent accounting source.

options.title: Prefer incremental fixes
options.body: Use the narrower identity and cache-invalidation approach, close this stack, and add only independently justified safeguards later.

recommendation.title: Adopt the lineage stack
recommendation.body: Review and land the dependency stack in order after exact-head frozen-corpus proof confirms compatibility, bounded operation, authorization transitions, and rollback.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and refined the current-main fork-accounting baseline and are best positioned to choose its permanent successor architecture.
